title: Plural negative questions: Eivätkö nämä ole…?
focus: Build plural negative yes/no questions with eivätkö and ole.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that means “Aren't the cars here?” Use ne autot (“the cars”) and täällä (“here”).
exercises.explanation: Eivätkö is the plural negative question form, and ole follows the subject. In English, start with “Aren’t” before the subject.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: negative question verb + demonstrative noun phrase subject + main verb after the negative question verb + location

parts.role: main verb after the negative question verb

optionFeedback.Eivätkö ne autot ole täällä?: Correct. Eivätkö carries plural negative agreement and -ko/-kö; ole follows later in the question.
optionFeedback.Eikö ne autot ole täällä?: “Eikö” is the singular negative question verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.
“Eivät” is the plural negative verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.
optionFeedback.Ovatko ne autot täällä?: “Ovatko” is the plural affirmative question verb; use “Eivätkö”, the plural negative question verb.

answerDiagnostics.category: Plural negative demonstrative questions: form not yet secure
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Eivätkö is the plural negative question form, and ole follows the subject. In English, start with “Aren’t” before the subject.
